FadR is a global regulator that controls the expression of genes involved not only in fatty acid and lipid biosynthesis, but also in the degradation of these compounds.

FadR is a global regulator of fatty acid and membrane lipid metabolism in E. coli and that it is required to coordinate the metabolism and homeostasis of the bacterial cell envelope during growth and starvation.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the regulation of fatty acid and lipid metabolism in E. coli, and the interplay between this metabolism and global regulation of gene expression.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the regulation of fatty acid metabolism during growth, ageing and starvation of E. coli.
the regulation of fatty acid and phosphatidylglycerol metabolism during the life cycle of E. coli.

FadR and the alarmones ppGpp and (cAMP) regulate the activities of enzymes involved in fatty acid metabolism and the expression of genes involved fatty acid and phospho lipid metabolism.

FadR and the global regulators of fatty acid metabolism are key players in the regulation of fatty acid metabolism in E. coli, that they are interconnected to the alarmones ppGpp and ppApp and that the fatty acids themselves are important regulators of their own metabolism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
FadR is not only a transcriptional regulator of fatty acid and phospho‐lipid metabolism but is also a key player in the regulation of the activities of enzymes involved in fatty acid metabolism.
the regulation of the FadR‐dependent genes is highly complex, and that the interconnections between the different regulators involved are not yet fully understood.
FadR and the global stress response are key players in maintaining the integrity and viability of E. coli cells during growth arrest.
